---
title: "Technical details"
---

quartodown generates a [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) website project from the
package sources, so the man pages, vignettes and generated pages are all Quarto
pages, and every Quarto feature works.

## How a build works

`quartodown::build_site()` runs in three stages:

1. **Before rendering**, it installs the package into a temporary library and
   writes a Quarto project into `_quarto/`. With `build_site(devel = TRUE)`,
   each page's R process loads it from source with `pkgload::load_all()`
   instead.[^devel]
2. **During rendering**, Quarto renders `_quarto/` into `docs/`, running the
   examples and vignette code against that package.
3. **After rendering**, it links code to its documentation and adds hover
   tooltips.

[^devel]: `devel = TRUE` may not work if your examples or vignettes start other
    R processes, for example with callr or parallel.

The only file you edit is `_quartodown.yml`. `_quarto/` is rewritten on every
build, and gitignored by `quartodown::use_quartodown()`:

```text
_quarto/
├── _quarto.yml                   # Quarto configuration (navbar, footer, theme)
├── index.md                      # home page
├── reference/
│   ├── index.qmd                 # function reference index
│   └── <topic>.qmd               # a page per man/*.Rd
├── authors.qmd                   # authors and citation page
├── vignettes/                    # the vignettes, as they are
├── man/figures/                  # images for the README and man pages
├── NEWS.md                       # changelog, with issues and users linked
├── quartodown.scss               # theme on top of Quarto's HTML
├── quartodown-header.html        # dark-mode default
└── quartodown-after-body.html    # navbar alignment
```

Reference pages are served at `reference/<topic>.html`, and `docs/pkgdown.yml`
lets [downlit](https://downlit.r-lib.org/) on other sites link to them.

## Before rendering

### The home page

`index.md` holds the README next to a sidebar with links, the license, the
citation, the developers and the README's badges.

A README `<picture>` with light and dark versions shows the one matching the
site's theme.

### The reference index

To group and order the function index, use the `reference:` field in
`_quartodown.yml`:

```yaml
reference:
  - title: Building the site       # <1>
    desc: >                        # <2>
      Set up a package, then build its site.
    contents:
      - use_quartodown             # <3>
      - starts_with("build_")      # <4>
```

1. Each entry becomes a section of the index, with this heading.
2. An optional description, shown under the heading.
3. A topic, by any of its `\alias{}` names.
4. A selector: `starts_with()`, `ends_with()`, `contains()`, `matches()`,
   `has_concept()`, `has_keyword()`, `-` to exclude and `c()` to combine.

`build_site()` warns about any topic the index leaves out, except
`\keyword{internal}` ones. An internal topic is listed, and gets a page, only
when named, as with roxygen's `reexports`, or selected with `internal = TRUE`,
as in `starts_with("dev_", internal = TRUE)`.

### The navbar and footer

The navbar links the "Get started" vignette, the reference index, the other
vignettes under "Articles" and the changelog. The footer has a "Developed by
..." line, built from `Authors@R`.

### Code output

R output is shown in the same block as the code, prefixed with `#>`, and left
out when copying the block. To show a chunk's output in a block of its own, set
`#| collapse: false` on it.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Changing the Quarto configuration

A `quarto:` field in `_quartodown.yml` is merged over the generated
configuration. Lists, like the navbar's items, are appended to; any other
setting is replaced, and `~` removes it. For example, to add a navbar link and
fold code blocks:

```yaml
quarto:
  website:
    navbar:
      right:
        - text: Blog
          href: https://example.com
  format:
    html:
      code-fold: true
```
:::

## The man pages

Each `man/*.Rd` file, except `\keyword{internal}` ones the [reference
index](#the-reference-index) doesn't list, becomes a reference page, rendered
with the package's Rd macros (such as Rdpack's `\insertRef{}`). Build-stage
`\Sexpr{}` macros run with the package installed, as in `R CMD build`, though
not with `devel = TRUE`. Examples run, with their output in the same block.

If `DESCRIPTION`'s `URL` includes a GitHub repository, each reference page and
vignette links to its source file under the title.

## After rendering

[downlit](https://downlit.r-lib.org/) links function calls in R code blocks, and
inline code like `mean()`, to their documentation. In blocks with [code
annotations](showcase.html#code-annotations), only function calls and `%op%`
operators such as `%in%` are linked.

References to the package's own functions also get a hover tooltip with their
usage and the first sentence of their description. Try it: hover over
`build_site()` or `use_quartodown()`. `build_site()` warns when a first sentence
is longer than 200 characters, since the tooltip cuts it off. To build without
tooltips, use `build_site(tooltips = FALSE)`.

## The theme

The site uses Quarto's `default` theme in light mode and `darkly` in dark mode,
with `quartodown.scss` on top of each:

```yaml
theme:
  light: [default, quartodown.scss]
  dark: [darkly, quartodown.scss]
```

The mode defaults to the browser's preference.
